key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings achieve better long-term corrosion and wear performance when the spray conditions promote disk-like droplets, dense lamellar microstructure, and low porosity.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing detonation spray parameters can improve protective coatings on carbon steel components operating in humid environments, extending service life under combined corrosion and tribological loading.
method: Prepared Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under varied spraying parameters
Compared coating droplet morphology, porosity, corrosion resistance, and tribological performance
Tested wear behavior across different humidity conditions with Si3N4 counterbodies
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic corrosion and tribology tests showing that coatings with fewer porosity defects had stronger long-term corrosion resistance, while friction coefficient and wear rate decreased as humidity increased.
watch_item: Performance is highly sensitive to porosity and spray-parameter control, so process inconsistency could offset the benefits of the amorphous coating.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
